title: G1 equal-weight prereg: burned-sessions manifest (v5 §4.7 rule 1)
prereg_rule: §4.7 data-hygiene rule 1: every paired session observed BEFORE the pilot-registration commit — including the ~4 unblinded pairs whose sigma_d informed the #485 provisional parameterization, and every session already analyzed in any memo — is permanently excluded from BOTH the calibration pilot AND the terminal series. The burned set is ENUMERATED in this committed manifest; the manifest, not prose, is the auditable object.
status_note: Pilot registration is NOT authorized yet (turnkey after epoch-5 refreeze per operator direction). This manifest is the enumeration required at the pilot-registration commit; it becomes binding when that commit freezes it and stamps pilot_registration_commit. Every entry below predates that future commit by construction (the burn boundary is DEFINED as the registration commit's timestamp, and the pilot manifest is prospective-only).

compiled_from.db_session_records: none — no *.db session records exist anywhere under the harness root (the per-arm runs.<tag>.db is only created inside an arm's native-live-run step; no surviving session reached that stage on disk). The JSON session records + logs above are therefore the complete two-arm session record set; there is no separate orchestrator DB carrying two-arm paired sessions.

session_convention_note: Per renquant-model#60's PIT parity backfill (cited by the epoch-3 EPOCH-NOTE and orchestrator doc/progress/2026-07-17-shadow-ab-epoch4-refreeze.md), ALL epoch-3-era paired sessions are schedule-mismatched under the close-anchored as-of contract and are not poolable with epoch-4+ sessions for any null fit. Additionally, 2026-07-11 and 2026-07-12 were not NYSE trading sessions (Saturday/Sunday; the trading-session gate landed only later on 2026-07-11 via orchestrator#488 review), so the three valid pairs re-observed Friday 2026-07-10's close — a zero-information paired world by the harness's own weekday-gate analysis.
completeness_note: Scope: this enumeration covers EVERY observed session, including sessions whose discrete records were overwritten by later same-date attempts and sessions that exist only in logs (session logs / launchd.err.log). The PART-B orchestrator telemetry (per-epoch/per-role counters) derives counts from RECORDED manifests alone — safe in direction (a session that left no record can never enter the pilot) but blind to overwritten/log-only sessions. This manifest, not the telemetry, is therefore the completeness surface for the burn set; compilation must sweep the logs, not just the record files. (Lesson: the 2026-07-11 09:43 PT epoch-3-minting valid pair was missed by the first compilation exactly because its discrete record had been overwritten; it was recovered from the session log, the freeze mint stamp, and its surviving sealed/per-arm artifacts.)
